definitionEn: a person who acts in a very stupid or thoughtless way
senseNote: Разговорное и грубоватое слово. О себе (I'm such an idiot!) звучит самоиронично, а в лицо другому — как оскорбление.
situation: Talking about someone, often yourself, who has just done something really stupid or careless.

examples.text: I felt like a complete [[idiot]] when I realised I'd sent the email to the whole company.
You'd have to be a real [[idiot]] to go hiking in the mountains without checking the forecast.
Our new manager treats us all like [[idiots]], explaining even the simplest tasks three times.

texts: Some [[idiot]] left the fridge door open all night, and the milk went off.
He's no [[idiot]]: he read every line of the contract before signing.
Only a total [[idiot]] would ride a motorbike without a helmet.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Полный идиот» по-английски — a complete, total или absolute idiot. Full с этим словом не сочетается.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Полный идиот» — a complete idiot (или total, absolute). Full — калька с «полный», а whole и deep с idiot не сочетаются.

nuance.text: "You [[idiot]], you've locked the keys in the car again!" my sister laughed.
nuance.explanationRu: В живой речи, даже в шутку, говорят you idiot. You fool звучит старомодно и театрально, как реплика из старой пьесы.

reverse.text: She's nobody's [[fool]]: she spotted the scam immediately.
reverse.explanationRu: Nobody's fool — устойчивое выражение: «её не проведёшь». С idiot его не строят.

fixIt.text: Some [[stupid]] has parked across our gate again, so I can't get the car out.
fixIt.explanationRu: Stupid — прилагательное, само по себе оно человека не обозначает. «Какой-то идиот» — some idiot.

wordFormation.text: Leaving the oven on all day was an [[idiotic]] mistake, and I paid for it.

reply.context: Your friend texts: "I just sent a message complaining about my boss — to my boss."
options: Oh no! That message was a complete idiot.
Oh no! You must feel like a complete idiot. Has she replied yet?
Regrettably, your conduct has been that of an idiot. Yours faithfully.
reply.explanationRu: Feel like a complete idiot — «чувствовать себя полным идиотом». Idiot — это человек, а не поступок или сообщение (глупость — idiocy). Третий ответ звучит как официальное письмо, а не сообщение другу.

definitionEn: lack of knowledge or information about something
situation: Describing a situation where someone does not know important facts, often causing mistakes or unfair judgements.

examples.text: Visitors who break local customs usually do it out of [[ignorance]], not rudeness.
Doctors say that much of the fear around the illness comes from [[ignorance]] about how it spreads.
I'm embarrassed to admit my [[ignorance]], but what exactly does a data analyst do?

texts: The accident was blamed on the driver's [[ignorance]] of local traffic rules.
The article exposed widespread [[ignorance]] about how pensions actually work.
She kept her parents in [[ignorance]] of her plans to quit university.

badCollocation.noteRu: Ignorance — «незнание». Если человек не отвечает на сообщения, это ignoring: I'm tired of her ignoring my messages.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ of the law is no excuse.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Ignorance of the law — «незнание закона». Ignoring — «игнорирование», illiteracy — «неграмотность», innocence — «невиновность».

nuance.text: Most people who break this rule do so out of [[ignorance]]: they simply don't know it exists.
nuance.explanationRu: Ignorance — незнание: человек просто не в курсе. Disregard — сознательное пренебрежение: знает, но не обращает внимания. Здесь люди не знают о правиле, поэтому подходит только ignorance.

reverse.text: The company showed a complete [[disregard]] for its workers' safety.
reverse.explanationRu: Компания знала о рисках и сознательно ими пренебрегла — это disregard for. Ignorance — именно незнание, и с for оно не сочетается.

fixIt.text: The survey revealed a shocking [[ignoring]] of geography: many adults couldn't find Canada on a map.
fixIt.explanationRu: Ignoring — «игнорирование», сознательное невнимание. Здесь люди просто не знают географию — это ignorance, незнание.

wordFormation.text: I'm completely [[ignorant]] about football, so please explain the offside rule.

reply.context: In a meeting, a colleague asks: "Does anyone know how the new expenses system works?"
options: Forgive my ignorance, but I didn't even know we had a new system.
No idea. Finance never answers my emails, so I'm treating them with ignorance now.
Total ignorance here, mate, no clue, lol.
reply.explanationRu: Forgive my ignorance — вежливое «простите мою неосведомлённость». Во втором ответе ignorance ошибочно значит «игнорирование» (это ignoring), а третий слишком небрежен для рабочей встречи.

rewrite.original: Most tourists break this rule because they simply don't know about it.
rewrite.frame: Most tourists break this rule out of ____.

definitionEn: language, pictures or symbols in art and writing that create vivid scenes in the mind
senseNote: Здесь — «образы, образность» в литературе и искусстве. Satellite imagery — «спутниковые снимки», это другое значение.
situation: Discussing how a poem, song, film or painting uses vivid descriptions or symbols to create pictures in your mind.

examples.text: The poem is full of dark [[imagery]]: storms, ruined towers and dying trees.
The director uses religious [[imagery]], such as candles and crosses, throughout the film.
Car adverts love the [[imagery]] of freedom: empty roads, mountains and endless sky.

texts: Her lyrics draw on the [[imagery]] of old fairy tales.
Critics praised the novel's striking [[imagery]] and simple, clear style.
Her photographs mix everyday objects with dreamlike [[imagery]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Imagery — неисчисляемое: beautiful imagery, без a. Про одну картинку говорят a beautiful image.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Rich in imagery — «богат образами». Image — одно изображение или имидж, imaging — съёмка (например, медицинская), portrait — портрет.

nuance.text: The advert's [[imagery]] (beaches, sunsets, smiling families) sells a dream rather than a product.
nuance.explanationRu: Imagery — вся совокупность образов: пляжи, закаты, семьи. Image — одно изображение или имидж; для целого ряда картинок нужно imagery.

reverse.text: The scandal has seriously damaged the bank's [[image]].
reverse.explanationRu: Репутация, «имидж» — image. Imagery — образы в искусстве и рекламе, а не репутация.

fixIt.text: The novel's [[imagination]] of burning forests and empty cities is hard to forget.
fixIt.explanationRu: Imagination — воображение, способность человека. Сами образы в тексте — imagery.

wordFormation.text: Poets often use the [[imagery]] of the seasons to write about growing old.

reply.context: In your book club chat, someone asks: "So what did everyone think of this week's poems?"
options: The imagery therein was deemed satisfactory by the undersigned.
Nice, but the poet's imagery on TV last night was really arrogant.
I loved the imagery. I could almost smell the sea in the second one.
reply.explanationRu: Imagery — образы в стихах, вплоть до запаха моря. Во втором ответе imagery ошибочно значит «имидж», а первый звучит как канцелярский отчёт, а не сообщение в чате.

definitionEn: extremely large in size, amount or degree
situation: Describing something so great in size, amount or importance that ordinary words like big seem too weak.

examples.text: Junior doctors work under [[immense]] pressure, and many leave the profession within five years.
From the plane we could see the [[immense]] forest stretching to the horizon in every direction.
The old letters turned out to be of [[immense]] value, and the museum paid a fortune for them.

texts: Building the bridge took [[immense]] skill and patience.
She takes [[immense]] pride in her garden.
Winning the award brought [[immense]] relief after years of rejection.

badCollocation.noteRu: Immense уже значит «огромный», поэтому very с ним не ставят. Говорят truly immense или просто immense.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Of immense importance — «огромной важности». Big и large с importance не сочетаются (калька с «большое значение»), heavy тоже.

nuance.text: The cathedral's [[immense]] dome can be seen from almost anywhere in the city.
nuance.explanationRu: Immense — огромный по размеру или количеству. Intense — сильный, напряжённый (жара, боль, чувства). Купол может быть огромным, но не «интенсивным».

reverse.text: After weeks of [[intense]] training, she was ready for the race.
reverse.explanationRu: Тренировки бывают напряжёнными — intense. Immense описывает размер или количество, а не силу и напряжённость.

fixIt.text: The storm caused [[big]] damage to farms across the region, costing millions.
fixIt.explanationRu: С damage не говорят big: это калька с «большой ущерб». Огромный ущерб — immense (или huge, serious) damage.

wordFormation.text: The show was [[immensely]] popular with teenagers in the nineties.

reply.context: Your colleague asks: "How did you feel when the project was finally finished?"
options: Honestly? Immense relief. I slept for eleven hours that night.
I felt a very immense happiness, to be honest.
Immense, but only a tiny bit.
reply.explanationRu: Immense relief — «огромное облегчение». Very immense — ошибка: слово уже означает крайнюю степень. А immense не может значить «чуть-чуть».

definitionEn: about to happen very soon, especially something unpleasant or dangerous
situation: Warning that something, usually bad or dangerous, is going to happen very soon, perhaps within hours or days.

examples.text: Residents were told to leave their homes because a flood was [[imminent]].
When the managers started holding secret meetings, staff realised that job cuts were [[imminent]].
Astronomers insist that the asteroid poses no [[imminent]] threat to Earth.

texts: Forecasters say heavy snow is [[imminent]] across the north.
Rumours of the band's [[imminent]] break-up spread quickly online.
Thousands of species are in [[imminent]] danger of extinction.

badCollocation.noteRu: «В ближайшем будущем» — in the near future. Imminent описывает само событие, которое вот-вот произойдёт: an imminent storm.

collocationTask.prompt: The historic theatre is in ___ danger of closing.
collocationTask.explanationRu: In imminent danger of — «под угрозой, которая вот-вот осуществится». Near и close о времени так не употребляют, а early danger — бессмыслица.

nuance.text: Passengers were told that boarding was [[imminent]] and asked to stay near the gate.
nuance.explanationRu: Imminent — «вот-вот начнётся». Inevitable — «неизбежный», но без указания, когда. Посадка на рейс не бывает «неизбежной»: важно, что она сейчас начнётся.

reverse.text: With costs rising every year, some price increases seem [[inevitable]] in the long run.
reverse.explanationRu: In the long run («в долгосрочной перспективе») противоречит imminent — «вот-вот». Для «когда-нибудь, но обязательно» нужно inevitable.

fixIt.text: Engineers warned that the dam was in [[eminent]] danger of bursting after the heavy rain.
fixIt.explanationRu: Eminent — «выдающийся, известный» (об учёном, враче). Опасность, которая вот-вот наступит, — imminent.

reply.context: Your colleague messages: "Is it true the office is moving to the other side of town?"
options: Affirmative. Relocation of personnel is imminent as per directive.
Looks like it. Apparently the announcement is imminent, maybe even this week.
Yes, but it's imminent, so probably not for another ten years.
reply.explanationRu: Imminent — «вот-вот, в ближайшие дни». «Лет через десять» ему противоречит, а первый ответ звучит как военный приказ, а не сообщение коллеге.

rewrite.original: Forecasters said that the hurricane would hit the coast within hours.
rewrite.frame: Forecasters said that the hurricane's arrival was ____.

definitionEn: the process of putting a plan, decision or system into action
situation: Talking about the stage when an agreed plan, law or new system actually starts being carried out in practice.

examples.text: The [[implementation]] of the new payroll software took six months and cost twice the budget.
The new recycling law is sensible, but its [[implementation]] has been slow and confusing.
Our group had great ideas, but our [[implementation]] was poor, so the final project disappointed our tutor.

texts: The report recommends the immediate [[implementation]] of stricter safety checks.
Hospital managers are responsible for the [[implementation]] of the new rules.
Poor [[implementation]] ruined what was actually a clever marketing plan.

badCollocation.noteRu: Мечта сбывается или осуществляется: the fulfilment (или realisation) of a dream. Implementation — о планах, решениях и системах.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Реформы и планы воплощают в жизнь — implementation. Embodiment и incarnation — «олицетворение», fulfilment — исполнение обещания или мечты.

nuance.text: The rules were introduced in January, but their [[implementation]] has been slow and patchy.
nuance.explanationRu: Introduction — момент, когда правило вводят. Implementation — постепенный процесс его применения на практике. Правила уже ввели в январе, а медленным бывает именно внедрение.

reverse.text: The [[introduction]] of smartphones changed the way people read the news.
reverse.explanationRu: Появление нового продукта — introduction. Implementation — выполнение плана или внедрение системы, а не появление смартфонов.

fixIt.text: The [[realisation]] of the new timetable caused chaos in the first week.
fixIt.explanationRu: Realisation в английском — прежде всего «осознание». «Реализация» плана, расписания или системы — implementation.

wordFormation.text: Delays in the [[implementation]] of the reform frustrated teachers and parents.

reply.context: At a team meeting, your manager says: "Everyone likes the plan. So what's our biggest risk now?"
options: Yo, the implementation thing is kinda sketchy, innit?
The biggest risk is the implementation of my summer holiday.
Implementation, I think. We've never rolled out anything this big before.
reply.explanationRu: Implementation — внедрение плана на практике, и это действительно главный риск. «Внедрение отпуска» — бессмыслица, а первый ответ слишком развязный для рабочей встречи.

rewrite.original: The company put the new system into practice without any problems.
rewrite.frame: The ____ of the new system went without any problems.

definitionEn: to lock someone up in jail, usually as a legal punishment
senseNote: Прямое значение — «заключать в тюрьму». В разговоре чаще говорят put in prison или jail.
situation: A court or government decides to lock a person up for a crime, or to keep someone captive.

examples.text: The journalist was [[imprisoned]] for six years after a trial that lasted just one day.
In the nineteenth century, people could be [[imprisoned]] simply for failing to pay their debts.
In the novel, the hero is wrongly [[imprisoned]] and spends years planning his revenge.

texts: Her grandfather was [[imprisoned]] for his political beliefs.
Nobody should be [[imprisoned]] without a fair trial.
The fraudster was [[imprisoned]] for stealing millions from pensioners.

badCollocation.noteRu: Срок указывают с for: imprisoned for five years. On здесь — калька с «на пять лет».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Imprisoned for twenty years — «провёл в тюрьме двадцать лет». Arrest — задержать, sentence to — приговорить к сроку, convict — признать виновным; с for twenty years они так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: After a two-day trial, he was [[imprisoned]] for eight years.
nuance.explanationRu: Arrest — задержание полицией, оно происходит до суда. Imprison — держать в тюрьме после приговора, поэтому «на восемь лет после суда» — только imprisoned.

reverse.text: Police [[arrested]] two men outside the bank late on Tuesday night.
reverse.explanationRu: Полиция задерживает, а в тюрьму сажает суд. Поэтому здесь arrested.

fixIt.text: During the war, the writer was [[sentenced]] in a cold, damp cell for almost two years.
fixIt.explanationRu: Sentence — «приговорить» (к сроку): sentenced to two years. Держать человека в камере — imprison: imprisoned in a cell.

rewrite.original: The court sent him to prison for ten years.

definitionEn: the punishment of being kept in jail for a period of time
situation: Talking about the punishment a court gives, when a person must spend a period of time locked in jail.

examples.text: The judge sentenced both men to five years' [[imprisonment]] for running the online scam.
After twenty years of [[imprisonment]], he had never used a smartphone or a cash machine.
Company directors who hide safety problems could face [[imprisonment]] under the new law.

texts: The crime carries a maximum penalty of ten years' [[imprisonment]].
The novel describes the hero's long [[imprisonment]] on a remote island.
Life [[imprisonment]] replaced the death penalty in many countries.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Пожизненное заключение» — life imprisonment (или a life sentence). Lifelong здесь — калька.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Пожизненное заключение — life imprisonment. Lifelong, entire и eternal с imprisonment в этом значении не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The film tells the story of her [[imprisonment]] and eventual escape.
nuance.explanationRu: Prison — место, здание тюрьмы. История заключения и побега — the story of her imprisonment; «her prison and escape» звучит так, будто речь о здании.

reverse.text: The old [[prison]] on the hill has been turned into a luxury hotel.
reverse.explanationRu: Здание тюрьмы — prison. Imprisonment — само наказание, его нельзя превратить в отель.

fixIt.text: She spent the first months of her [[conclusion]] writing letters to her children.

wordFormation.text: Years of [[imprisonment]] had left him pale, thin and nervous in crowds.

rewrite.original: He spent ten years in prison for the robbery.
rewrite.frame: He was sentenced to ten years' ____ for the robbery.
rewrite.explanationRu: Ten years' imprisonment — «десять лет лишения свободы».

definitionEn: the fact that someone cannot do something
situation: Explaining that a person or organisation cannot manage to do something, often a problem that causes trouble.

examples.text: His [[inability]] to say no means he always ends up doing other people's work.
Investors were worried by the company's [[inability]] to explain where the money had gone.
Chronic stress can lead to an [[inability]] to concentrate, even on simple tasks.

texts: Her [[inability]] to swim kept her away from the beach.
The report blamed the council's [[inability]] to act quickly.
An [[inability]] to sleep is often the first sign of stress.

badCollocation.noteRu: После inability ставят инфинитив: inability to pay. Of + -ing здесь — ошибка.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Неспособность справиться — inability to cope. Impossibility описывает саму ситуацию, disability — инвалидность, incompetence — некомпетентность; с to cope их не употребляют.

nuance.text: His [[inability]] to make decisions drives his colleagues mad.
nuance.explanationRu: Disability — инвалидность, физическое или психическое ограничение. Inability to do something — просто неспособность что-то сделать, как нерешительность этого коллеги.

reverse.text: The charity helps people with a physical [[disability]] find work.
reverse.explanationRu: Об инвалидности говорят disability. Inability всегда требует уточнения, что именно человек не может: inability to walk.

fixIt.text: The firm's [[impossibility]] to pay its suppliers eventually led to bankruptcy.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Невозможность заплатить» — калька. О человеке или компании говорят inability to pay; impossibility описывает саму ситуацию: the impossibility of the task.

reply.context: Your manager asks: "Why didn't you reply to the client's email yesterday?"
options: Due to inability, like, stuff happened, you know?
Sorry, the system was down, and my inability to log in held everything up.
I had a great inability to write it. It was my best email ever.
reply.explanationRu: My inability to log in — «я не мог войти в систему». Inability — неспособность, а не талант, а первый ответ слишком небрежный и бессвязный для разговора с начальником.

rewrite.original: He can't concentrate, and this worries his teachers.
rewrite.explanationRu: Inability to + инфинитив: his inability to concentrate.

definitionEn: not enough, or not good enough, for what is needed
senseNote: Здесь — «недостаточный, неудовлетворительный». Не путайте с русским «неадекватный» (о странном поведении): это скорее irrational или out of line.
situation: Complaining that the money, staff, equipment or explanation provided is not sufficient or not of acceptable quality.

examples.text: The hospital's staffing levels are dangerously [[inadequate]], according to a new report.
The flat was cheap, but the heating was completely [[inadequate]] for a Siberian winter.
The teacher said my answer was [[inadequate]] because I hadn't supported it with any evidence.

texts: Many schools still have [[inadequate]] funding for science labs.
The airline's apology was [[inadequate]], so I complained again.
Two bathrooms for forty guests is simply [[inadequate]].

badCollocation.noteRu: «Неадекватный сосед» по-английски — an unpredictable или a difficult neighbour. Inadequate значит «недостаточный, не отвечающий требованиям».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Woefully inadequate — «удручающе, совершенно недостаточный». Strongly, heavily и highly с inadequate не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The heating was [[inadequate]], so we wore coats in the office all winter.
nuance.explanationRu: Inadequate — недостаточный по количеству или качеству: тепла просто не хватало. Inappropriate — неуместный, неподходящий для ситуации; об отоплении так не говорят.

reverse.text: Wearing shorts to a job interview would be [[inappropriate]].
reverse.explanationRu: Шорты на собеседовании неуместны — inappropriate. Inadequate значит «недостаточный» и к одежде в этом смысле не подходит.

fixIt.text: The school's science labs are [[unsatisfied]] for a modern curriculum.
fixIt.explanationRu: Unsatisfied описывает людей, которые чем-то недовольны. О недостаточном оборудовании говорят inadequate.

wordFormation.text: The report highlighted the [[inadequacy]] of flood defences in the region.

reply.context: A colleague complains: "We've got one printer for sixty people, and it breaks every week."
options: I know. And the IT guy is so inadequate: he laughs at his own jokes all day.
One must concede that the printing provision is somewhat inadequate, sir.
I know. One printer is totally inadequate for an office this size.
reply.explanationRu: Totally inadequate — «совершенно недостаточно». В первом ответе inadequate использовано как русское «неадекватный» (странный), а второй звучит слишком чопорно для разговора с коллегой.
